item.title: [British Journal of Anaesthesia] Genotype-phenotype relationships in butyrylcholinesterase deficiency: a genotypic approach should be the gold standard. Comment on Br J Anaesth 2026; 137: 450–9
item.description: We read with interest the systematic review by Snak de Souza and colleagues1 regarding genotype-phenotype relationships in butyrylcholinesterase deficiency. As the authors emphasise, the phenotypic approach traditionally used to screen for and characterise butyrylcholinesterase (BChE) variants has several inherent limitations. These include the limited number of laboratories performing such assays, the lack of standardised testing procedures, reduced accuracy in cases of variants associated with markedly decreased BChE activity, and difficulties interpreting results for compound heterozygotes.
